title: A Prom for the Recipe
premise: Ines Zhou has spent three years perfecting the art of invisibility—cooking dinner, checking homework, and keeping her siblings fed while their mother works hospital night shifts. When her best friend Priya vanishes, leaving only a janitor's keyring stamped with the school's old boiler-room number, Ines discovers the keys open a ledger documenting how Coach Danner and Principal Whitlock have been quietly extorting scholarship athletes for years. To expose them, Ines must join the academic decathlon team her friend secretly captained and win the state title that grants its members a public platform—and survive the season's final basketball game, where Danner plans to bury the evidence forever. Ines wins both championships, but justice comes at a cost: she loses her invisibility, nearly loses her family's fragile stability, and learns that some prices, once paid, can't be refunded.
about_author: V. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former night-shift line cook who wrote this debut on bus rides between double shifts. They live somewhere with bad weather and good diners, and they still keep a jar of orphaned keys on their windowsill.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Small Things
chapters.summary: Ines Zhou's POV. A Tuesday in the Zhou household: rice stretched across five appetites, homework checked at the kitchen table, Mom's scrubs already on by 9 p.m. Ines runs the house like a quiet machine and likes it that way. Emotional beat: competence as armor—we see exactly what Ines stands to lose.

chapters.title: Priya's Empty Seat
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Priya doesn't show at their usual lunch spot, then misses decathlon practice, then doesn't answer for two days. The school shrugs; Priya's parents assume she's staying with friends. Only Ines notices the text Priya sent at 11:47 p.m.: 'found something. don't let them know i know.' Emotional beat: dread arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A padded envelope arrives, no return address: Priya's spare keyring, six keys, one brass tag stamped B-7—the decommissioned boiler room. Ines's little brother Marcus dares her to use them; her sister Lulu begs her not to. That night Ines pockets the keys instead of sleeping. Emotional beat: the moment a bystander becomes a participant.

chapters.title: B-7
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, tense and sensory. The boiler room smells of rust and old paper. Behind a loose panel: a green ledger of payments—athletes' families 'donating' to keep scholarships, Coach Danner's initials on every page, and a second list titled 'witnesses.' Priya's name is third. Emotional beat: vertigo—the school she trusted is a machine with gears made of people.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She learns Priya was quietly running the academic decathlon team—a joke to everyone but the state committee, whose winning captain gets a televised interview slot. A platform. Ines tries out on impulse and bombs the math round, but Coach Okafor sees something in her composure. Emotional beat: grief converted into a plan.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Head Down
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Danner starts watching her—friendly at first, offering to 'help the family out,' a wordless reminder he knows about her free-lunch status. Ines plays dumb while photographing ledger pages on a cracked phone. Marcus covers her absences; Lulu notices everything. Emotional beat: the corruption begins pricing her silence.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Took the Deal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Theo Marsh, star forward, scholarship kid, one of the ledger's names. He warns Ines off in the parking lot—not cruelly, desperately. His mother's medical bills are the leash. He gives her one true detail: Priya came to him first, and he said no. Emotional beat: complicity as survival, the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Practice Makes Liars
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Decathlon drills by day, ledger translation by night—she maps the money like a recipe, ingredient by ingredient. Okafor pushes the team hard, sensing Ines is running from something. Lulu finds the keys and forces a confrontation: 'You're becoming Mom's parent and nobody's kid.' Emotional beat: the home front cracks under the secret.

chapters.title: What Priya Knew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following the ledger's pattern, Ines tracks down Priya's cousin, who reveals Priya had been recording interviews with affected families—audio files backed up to an account only accessible via a recovery code hidden in Priya's half of a shared notebook. The notebook is in the school library's lost-and-found archive. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Archive Is Closed
chapters.summary: Ines and Theo's POV, alternating. The archive room was re-keyed last week—Danner's order. Theo agrees to get Ines in through the athletics corridor during Friday's game, his guilt finally tipping into action. First real alliance, sealed with mutual distrust. Emotional beat: two compromised people choosing each other anyway.

chapters.title: Halftime
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, kinetic. During halftime chaos, Theo badges Ines into the corridor. She retrieves the notebook—but Danner catches them in the stairwell. He doesn't threaten; he offers. Full ride for Theo's brother, tutoring stipend for Ines, 'and we forget the girl who ran away.' Ines says nothing. Theo says yes. Emotional beat: the price of survival, itemized.

chapters.title: The Recipe
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the kitchen table, Ines decodes Priya's cipher—it's built from their childhood recipe card game, ratios standing in for letters. The audio files exist, complete, damning. But playing them means exposing every family on the ledger, including Theo's. Ines faces the central choice: justice for all or protection for the few. Emotional beat: the weight of other people's names.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The decathlon regionals—chaotic, exhilarating, the first thing in weeks that belongs entirely to Ines. The team qualifies for states. Danner attends, applauding, a message in the applause. Afterward he tells her Whitlock knows about the boiler room visit. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the closing trap.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, intimate. Mom's shift was cut; she's home at dawn and finds the ledger photocopies. Instead of anger: her own story—how a factory boss once held her immigration paperwork, and how she chose silence to keep her kids fed. 'I won't tell you what to do,' she says. 'But know what it costs either way.' Emotional beat: inheritance of fear, offered and refused.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Danner reneges—his brother's ride was always contingent on total loyalty, and Danner now suspects Theo helped Ines. Theo finds his locker emptied of his recruiting letters. Cornered, he comes to Ines with everything he's been holding back: recordings of his own. Emotional beat: the deal's true face revealed; rage as fuel.

chapters.title: A Call From Priya
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A burner call: Priya is alive, hiding with an aunt two states away after Danner threatened her family. She's terrified but lucid, and she confirms the files are authentic—then asks Ines to stop, afraid of what exposure does to the families. Ines must decide whether to honor her friend's fear or her friend's original mission. Emotional beat: love versus justice, no clean side.

chapters.title: States
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The state championship. Ines competes like someone with nothing left to protect, and wins—the televised interview slot is hers, scheduled for the morning after the final basketball game. Danner watches her accept the trophy with a smile that promises consequences. Emotional beat: the platform secured; the clock now audible.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating Ines/Theo POV, propulsive. Championship night. Danner plans to incinerate the ledger originals in the boiler room during the game's final quarter—the building empty, the story buried. Ines and Theo split up: Theo keeps Danner talking courtside while Ines races to B-7 with her phone recording. Emotional beat: everything converging, breath held.

chapters.title: Fire Needs Three Things
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climax. In the boiler room, Whitlock catches her—then falters when Ines plays Priya's audio: his own voice, negotiating. Danner arrives; a standoff over the burning barrel; Theo appears with security, having tipped off a school-board member using the ledger copies. The originals burn, but the copies and recordings are already beyond reach. Emotional beat: the fire takes the past, not the future.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The televised interview. Ines goes off-script, names no one recklessly, but holds up the keyring and tells the story of a girl who found something and wouldn't stay found. District investigators move within days; Danner resigns mid-investigation; Whitlock is suspended. Families on the ledger begin receiving restitution. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, handed carefully into the law's hands.

chapters.title: Priya Comes Home
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Priya returns—angry that Ines exposed the families, grateful that it worked, unable to be either fully. Their friendship survives as something new: honest, scarred. Theo's brother gets his ride through legitimate channels; Theo transfers schools with his head up. Emotional beat: repair without erasure.

chapters.title: Dinner at Six
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, coda. A normal Tuesday again—rice, homework, Mom home by nine because shifts got better. Ines hangs the brass B-7 tag above the stove, next to Priya's recipe cards. She's visible now at school, and it costs something daily, and she pays it. Final beat: the price of survival was high, but so is the price of silence—and Ines has learned which bill she'd rather carry.
